documents.label: Personality, Strengths & Blind Spots
documents.body: 5. My Personality Profile Myers-Briggs: ENTJ-A ("The Commander") Big Five / OCEAN: Very high Conscientiousness (114) & Extraversion (109); very low Agreeableness (61) & Neuroticism (39). As in, top 1-5% most extreme for all four. Gallup CliftonStrengths: My dominant themes are in the Influencing and Executing domains. Image Achiever: I work hard and possess a great deal of stamina. I take immense satisfaction in being busy and productive. I love to complete tasks, and my accomplishments fulfill me. I have a strong inner drive — an innate source of intensity, energy and power that motivates me to work hard to get things done. Arranger: I can organize, but also have a flexibility that complements this ability. I like to determine how all of the pieces and resources can be arranged for maximum productivity. I have a natural ability to coordinate people and resources for maximum effectiveness. My creative flexibility in complex situations leads to greater efficiency. Learner: I have a great desire to learn and want to continuously improve. The process of learning, rather than the outcome, excites me. I provide your teammates with a logical perspective on things. Competition: I measure my progress against the performance of others. I strive to win first place and revel in contests. I motivate yourself and others to a higher standard of performance. I can raise a group’s achievement level by creating a culture of winning and aspiring to be the best. Significance: I want to make a big impact. I am independent and prioritize projects based on how much influence they will have on your organization or people around me. I want to do important work and are determined to make a difference. I want others to respect me for my significant contribution and willingness to work hard to achieve success. BIS-11: Very low impulsiveness (41). In practice, this means: I am a mission-oriented, systems-builder energized by ambitious goals and rational debate. I thrive on turning chaos into order and driving a team toward a clear, world-changing objective. My (very) high disagreeableness is a feature of my commitment to the mission. I believe that intellectual honesty and rigorous debate are the fastest path to the best ideas. 6. My Strengths My Gallup profile shows my talents are concentrated in Influencing and Executing. You should leverage me accordingly. My Gallup profile concentrates in Influencing and Executing — but my impact comes from how these combine with my drive for Significance. Leverage me accordingly. Influencing ~ "the catalyst" First-principles: I love rigorous, first-principles debate. I build cases methodically and am effective at rallying alignment behind a mission. Inspiring action: I articulate compelling visions that energize teams and partners. Taking charge: I love stepping into chaos, making tough calls, and creating clarity where there is none. I thrive under pressure. Executing ~ "the architect" Making things happen: My instinct is to turn ideas into action. I have a deep-seated need to see tangible progress every day. Organizing complexity: I break down large, complex challenges into elegant systems and processes. This is where my obsession with systems-building lives. Raising the bar: I create cultures of winning – measuring progress, celebrating milestones, and pushing the team toward a higher standard. Strategic thinking ~ "the philosopher" Learning & synthesizing: I am a relentless learner, constantly pulling ideas from disparate fields to find integrative insights. Seeing the future: I often live 1-3 years ahead, anticipating challenges and opportunities before they arrive. Holding paradoxes: I often hold two opposing ideas in tension and still act decisively. Integrative thinking is a core skill. Relationship-building ~ "the connector" Superconnector: I love mapping social graphs and making catalytic introductions that create value for all involved. Culture creator: I design rituals, spaces, and shared experiences that compound trust and belonging over time. Coalition builder: I align talent, capital, and culture behind one mission – and create co-ownership so wins feel shared. 7. My Blind Spots (Where I Need Your Help) I cannot see my own blind spots. I am counting on you to be part of my feedback loop. My commitment: if you name it, I will own it. Control creep: My default is to do it myself, especially on things I used to own. This makes me a bottleneck. Help me: Proactively own your domain. If I'm creeping into your weeds, say: "Chappy, I've got this. Let me come back with a finished product." I’ll recognize it as gift, not a challenge. Intensity: My energy and ambition can feel overwhelming. Not everyone operates at 3am-wake-up, vision-quest intensity – and I can inadvertently make others feel they're not keeping up. Help me: Tell me if my pace is unsustainable for you. High performance AND psychological safety aren't opposites. Impatience: I have a high internal clock. When things feel slow, I push for shortcuts that skip necessary deliberation. Help me: Make the case for slowing down. Say: "I think we need one more day to de-risk this. Here's why." Over-structured: I love systems and process. But sometimes situations call for fluidity, improvisation, or just vibing – and I can be too rigid when looseness would serve better. Help me: "This one doesn't need a framework – let's just riff." Over-scheduled (120%): I tend to pack my todo list beyond capacity, leaving no slack for serendipity, spontaneous connection, or the unexpected opportunities that often matter most. Help me: If you see something worth my time, push for it.

documents.label: How We Collaborate
documents.body: 8. My Time & Availability Working hours: I am effectively always working (usually 80-100 h/w 😅), but my core, most responsive hours are 9am - 7pm PT. You can expect me to be highly engaged during this window. (Curious? Check out Chappy’s Core Daily Routine) Weekends: My mornings before 9am, as well as Tuesday and Thursday afternoons, are my protected deep work blocks (eg. coding, writing, researching, strategy). I will be slow to respond during these blocks. I work intensely on weekends, but I cherish this time for uninterrupted, creative deep work. Please respect this by avoiding non-urgent requests. 9. Meetings Philosophy: I believe meetings are for two things: 1) high-bandwidth debate to solve a hard problem, and 2) efficient, team-wide status updates and alignment. Expectations: Come on time & prepared: I expect the meeting leader to arrive on time and with a clear, written agenda. Active participation: I expect everyone on the call to be engaged and to contribute. The meeting leader is responsible for creating and facilitating these conditions. Pre-reads: A pre-read the night before is a gift to everyone in the meeting. It's by no means required, but it is always appreciated and allows us to use our synchronous time for the highest-value discussions.

documents.label: Communication
documents.body: Note on my response time: I am juggling a very high volume of open lines (often 100+ at a time). While I will see your message, it may occasionally take me 3-7 days to respond to non-urgent pings. Please do not take this personally; it is a function of my system for managing focus. If you need a faster response, read on! 10. My Communication Principles Async-first: I believe the best work happens in long, uninterrupted blocks of focus. For any complex topic, my strong preference is to start with a written, well-structured document (like a Notion or Google Doc). This allows me to engage with your ideas deeply on my own schedule and it forces clarity of thought for everyone involved. High signal-to-noise ratio: Be concise. Use bullet points. Get to the point quickly and put your recommendation or key question at the very top. I trust you've done the deep thinking; you don't need to show all your work in the initial message. Minimal ChatGPT fluff please! Context is your responsibility: Before you ask for my input, ask yourself: "Does Chappy have all the context he needs to make a decision on this in under two minutes?" If no, provide the necessary background links or a one-sentence summary. Reducing friction for me is the fastest way to get a response. Default to transparency: Whenever possible, our communications should happen in shared, public channels within the team. This reduces redundant conversations, creates a shared context, and allows others to learn and contribute. 11. The Right Channel for the Job For non-urgent, day-to-day comms & FYIs: Use the appropriate public Slack channel. If you need my specific input, you must @ me or I will likely miss it. I am in over 100 channels and rely on mentions to filter what's important. To get my input on a document: Share a Notion or Google Doc with me and @ me in a specific channel with a clear question and your recommendation. This ensures it hits my radar. To pitch me a new, big idea: Write a concise, one-page document outlining: 1) the problem, 2) the proposed solution, and 3) a concrete first step. Share this with me via Slack. For an urgent, time-sensitive issue (≤ 3 hours): Send me a text message prefixed with "URGENT:". This will get my immediate attention. My phone # is included in my email signature and on my Slack profile.

documents.label: Feedback
documents.body: 12. How to Give Me Feedback I am running a thousand miles an hour and have multiple blind spots. I consider it a core part of your job to help me see them. Your honest perspective is a gift that helps me, and the entire mission, get better. The method: (a https://books.chappyasel.com/crucial-conversations framework) Ask for permission: Because I am constantly context-switching, the most effective way to give me feedback is to first get my attention. A simple Slack message like, "Hey Chappy, do you have 10 minutes for some feedback on X later today?" is the perfect way to start. This allows me to switch into the right mental frame to actually hear you. Lead with the facts: Start with a neutral, specific observation. (eg. "In the leadership sync yesterday, when we discussed the budget, I noticed we moved to a decision without hearing from the broader team.") Share Your story: Explain the impact this had on you or the project. (eg. "The story I told myself was that we are prioritizing speed over rigor in our financial planning, which makes me concerned about future risks.") End with a question: Open the door for a real conversation. (eg. "I was hoping you could help me understand your thinking there?") The golden rule: I deeply value feedback that is well-reasoned, specific, and delivered with the clear intent of improving our mission. You will always be rewarded for courage and candor, and using the method above will ensure your feedback lands with maximum impact. 13. How I Give Feedback My philosophy: (from https://books.chappyasel.com/radical-candor) My goal is always to care personally while challenging directly. My feedback is never personal; it is an investment in your growth because I believe in your potential and I want you, and the team, to succeed at the highest level. How I recognize great work I believe that recognition is a critical part of a high-performance culture. My goal is to ensure you feel seen and valued for your contributions. How I show it: Succinct public praise: I frequently give public praise for specific, excellent work, especially in our Slack channels or team meetings. My style is often succinct and direct, but it is a sincere acknowledgment of a job well done. Trust and autonomy: The single greatest way I show my respect for your work is by giving you more of it. When you consistently deliver with excellence, I will respond by giving you more ownership, more freedom, and bigger, more interesting problems to solve. Advocacy: I will champion you and your work in the rooms you are not in. I will use my network and my platform to create opportunities for you and to ensure your contributions are recognized by the people who matter.

documents.label: Hobbies
documents.body: I have two hobbies and I take both of them very seriously! Bodybuilding (Natural) Outside of tech, I live a second life as a natural bodybuilder! I’ve trained with intent and intensity for 8+ years and occasionally compete in the INBF/WNBF natural federations. I track every set, iterate my programming, and measure what matters – I even built my own app to systematize progress! One reason I love lifting is the objective daily affirmation: I walk in, hit a PR, and know definitely that I’m the best I’ve ever been! :weightlifting-app: Weightlifting App: my app for tracking and analyzing workouts “From Nerd to Bodybuilder” (article): the story linking my tech mindset to lifting @boyswithgains (fitness Instagram): progress logs, training clips, show prep, etc. Image Reading I am a bibliomaniac. I read 50-100 books a year, and much of my personal and professional philosophy is a synthesis of frameworks from thinkers I deeply respect. If you want to understand the "why" behind how I operate, these books are the source material! Read my full compendium of book notes here: https://books.chappyasel.com/ A few fun reading lists… On Personal Growth & Effectiveness https://books.chappyasel.com/7-habits-of-highly-effective-people: The bible and foundational operating system for a principled and effective life. https://books.chappyasel.com/thinking-fast-and-slow: The essential guide to understanding our own cognitive biases and making better, more rational decisions. https://books.chappyasel.com/atomic-habits: The tactical operating system for building the small, consistent habits that lead to remarkable results. https://books.chappyasel.com/plays-well-with-others: How to build and maintain the strong personal and professional relationships that are the foundation of a happy and impactful life. https://books.chappyasel.com/range: The intellectual justification for my "paradoxical passions" and my belief in the power of being a T-shaped, cross-disciplinary thinker. https://books.chappyasel.com/barking-up-the-wrong-tree: A data-driven guide (my favorite) to what actually leads to a successful and meaningful life, challenging many common assumptions. Community & Events https://books.chappyasel.com/bowling-alone: The definitive diagnosis of the problem we are trying to solve: the collapse of community and social capital in the modern world. This is the "why" behind our in-person focus. https://books.chappyasel.com/the-art-of-community: Provides the core principles for building a community with a strong identity, clear boundaries, and meaningful rituals. https://books.chappyasel.com/community: A powerful philosophical argument that the key to a thriving society is structuring belonging and citizen-led action, which is the heart of the AIC's grassroots model. https://books.chappyasel.com/the-art-of-gathering: Our tactical bible for event design. It's why we obsess over having a clear purpose for every single event we host, from a small dinner to a large festival. https://books.chappyasel.com/the-2-hour-cocktail-party: A masterclass in simple, repeatable, and high-energy event formats. It's the "how-to" guide for much of what our chapters do. On Building High-Performance Teams https://books.chappyasel.com/the-culture-code: My primary playbook for architecting a culture of psychological safety, shared vulnerability, and purpose. All of the leaders around me have also read this book. https://books.chappyasel.com/radical-candor: The non-negotiable framework for how we give feedback. It's about caring personally while challenging directly. https://books.chappyasel.com/thanks-for-the-feedback: The user manual for how to receive feedback – even when it's poorly delivered – as a gift for personal growth. https://books.chappyasel.com/crucial-conversations: The tactical guide for navigating the high-stakes, emotionally charged conversations that are inevitable when doing ambitious work. On Building a World-Changing Mission https://books.chappyasel.com/life-3-0 & https://books.chappyasel.com/the-singularity-is-near: These are the foundational texts that ignited my obsession and defined the core mission of The AI Collective. https://books.chappyasel.com/zero-to-one: The definitive guide to thinking from first principles and building something truly new in the world. https://books.chappyasel.com/start-with-why: The core of how I think about inspiring a movement – it's not about what we do, but why we do it. https://books.chappyasel.com/the-infinite-game: This book shapes our long-term strategy. We are building a resilient organization with a just cause, designed to last for generations. Image

documents.label: Why So Early?
documents.body: Origin story: Growing up, I was very definitively a night owl. It wasn’t until cutting for my bodybuilding competition when my hormones got thrown out of whack that I started naturally (uncontrollably) waking up at 4am, 3am, and sometimes even 2am wired 😅. Ever since mid-2022, I made the transition and haven’t looked back! Why wake up extremely early? The benefits are near-endless but here are a few of my favorites: It’s easy, actually It’s really not that hard to wake up early. Fundamentally, I’m still sleeping the same amount as anyone else would, I’m just shifting my schedule earlier. Commit to it for a couple of weeks and watch your circadian rhythm naturally shift! I get 3+ hours completely to myself That means you’re fully in control of your schedule and no-one can disturb you! I try to allocate as much of this time as I can to “eating the frog” – working on the day’s biggest and most important project Once the meetings + comms bombardment starts, my plate gets filled up will small yet urgent tasks which can easily engulf the rest of my day I can’t miss a workout When I work out this early in the morning before all meeting, it’s nearly impossible to make an excuse to miss it (not that working out too little is ever an issue 😅) I only have to shower once There are naturally two points where I have to shower daily: once after my workout and once before my meetings. Why not line the two up?! I have enough time This gives me enough time to work out early in the morning, shower, and get going My benchmark is at least 4 hours between waking and first meeting. That’s the minimum I can fit my full morning routine into and not feel too rushed I naturally out-work everyone By starting work before 4am every morning, most people’s 9-5 becomes my 12-hour work day. The inertia naturally becomes that I out-work everyone!

documents.label: Wake Up
documents.body: Alarm goes off (Apple Watch) and smart lights turn on (dimmed) Immediately after waking, stand up to get blood flowing Head to the bathroom to weigh in. Record daily weight on spreadsheet Put on workout clothes, which were laid out the night before Hop back into bed to increase body temperature Turn on light therapy lamp to imitate sunrise I find that 30+ mins of this significantly improves my morning alertness 🦞 OpenClaw sends a brief at 4am with agenda for the day, complete with background research on every meeting and task for the day. Social media posts + interactions are drafted. Review my quarterly + weekly goals and ✅ daily todo list (Sunsama) and read a few morning emails and texts to prime for the day

documents.label: Pre-Workout
documents.body: Try to wait 30m+ after waking before drinking pre-workout (with two Alpha GPC pills) See ☕ Caffeine Ideally, I wait 60-90 mins before starting to ingest caffeine. This helps to reduce mid-afternoon drowsiness immensely. Though it’s a delicate balance between that and being lethargic in the morning or even falling back asleep accidentally. “Eat the frog” – jump straight into the highest-priority project of the day before other urgent matters get in the way

documents.label: Move To Desk
documents.body: After 1.5 hours, body temperature is high enough to move to desk Make my bed. Every single day without exception. This is the first big ☑️ which sets up a highly productive day full of ☑️s! After finishing first ~300mg of caffeine, top up with another 400mg or so and drink that over the next ~30 mins. Also mixed in is 15-20g creatine, 15g beta alanine, 10-30g HydroPrime glycerol.

documents.label: Lift
documents.body: BUZZING! Head to the gym to get an hour-long lift in! Refill blender bottle with water, electrolytes (Mio), lemon juice, and a tiny bit more caffeine as a home-brewed, low-calorie substitute for Gatorade! I use Weightlifting App – an app I built myself that’s about as analytics-heavy as a lifting app can get! Check it out 💪 Music 🎶: want to get HYPE? Listen to a mix in my RAGE or HARDcore Soundcloud playlists! Why do I lift in the morning? I can consume as much caffeine as I want! As opposed to working out in the afternoon where I have to be weary about consuming too much caffeine and not being able to sleep at night. Caffeine consumed while fasting and shortly after waking hits like no other! The morning endorphins release sets up the rest of the day perfectly I have to shower before my morning meetings. If I don’t work out then as well, that means I have to shower twice a day. Instead, I can stack the two together and save myself a bunch of time! I usually have the gym all to myself which means I can use whatever equipment I want! Packed gyms are no fun

documents.label: Work
documents.body: Return to work! This is some of my most productive time of the day as I have endorphins flowing and dawn is just starting to break. People still aren’t generally awake so I still have this time to myself!

documents.label: Shower
documents.body: Head to shower before the sweat soaks in too much 😅 Shampoo + facial cleanser at the same time → conditioner + body wash at the same time, leave each on for 1 min Blow dry hair, deodorant, Eau de Perfume, trim beard, shave, brush teeth, chapstick, facial moisturizer, facial caffeine solution, body moisturizer, sunscreen, hair product ↑ Great time to listen to an audiobook! Also easy to stop morning routine and take notes

documents.label: “Breakfast”
documents.body: Take morning stack! See 💊 Supp Stacks Prepare a protein shake with water base, 1 scoop whey isolate (30g protein), 1/2 scoop collagen peptides, 1/2 scoop PB2 Crunchy, and a scoop of greens powder (~300 cals) Down both while either 1) watching the sun continue to rise and listening to a podcast or 2) at my desk working if I have meetings coming up

documents.label: PM Prep
documents.body: Set up everything for a perfect PM! Clean blender bottles and fill with hot water to avoid having to dish wash Refill 2 pre-workout blender bottles with 1) 400mg Gorilla Mode pre-workout, 2) 10-15g creatine, 3) 10g beta alanine and place on bedside stand (along with two Alpha GPC pills) Lay out micropore mouth tape and nasal strip on bedside stand See https://books.chappyasel.com/breath Lay out tomorrow’s workout outfit next to bed Why? To absolutely minimize friction for tomorrow!

documents.label: Sunset
documents.body: Smart lights automatically dim and yellow to match sunset. This creates an environment that encourages the release of melatonin, prepping the body for sleep This is also shortly after dinner (if I’m eating dinner that day), so I start feeling a little more drowsy as digestion kicks in I generally switch to less cognitively demanding tasks around now, eg. responding to texts and emails or personal / reflective tasks 🦞 OpenClaw sends a daily recap at 7pm with summaries of the day’s meetings, complete with aggregated next steps and drafts for followup emails / texts.

documents.label: Wind Down
documents.body: Review my day: ✅ daily todo list, score the day (-2, -1, 0, +1, or +2 with note) mentally walk through tomorrow Take night stack ~45m before sleep See 💊 Supp Stacks Smart lights automatically adjust to 30% brightness 45m before sleep Sometime in the next 45m, perform sleep routine: Brush teeth, go to the bathroom Fill 40oz Hydroflask with iced water, Mio zero-cal flavoring, and lemon juice Adjust smart lights to 10% brightness (sleep scene) Spray a nice scent on the bed and around the room (Febreze Air Ocean) Boxers, no PJs AirPods for listening to an audiobook

documents.label: Sleep
documents.body: Put on a comfy sleep mask for complete darkness Put on micropore mouth tape and nasal strip to encourage healthy nasal breathing See https://books.chappyasel.com/breath Switch to a background podcast (eg. Lex Fridman) Yes, I fall asleep wearing them 😅 Ensure alarm is set for the proper wakeup time / sleep duration (depending on priority) Varies (5h-7.5h, avg. 6.25h) depending on weight. See 💤 Sleep Duration

documents.label: Sinusoidal vs Square-wave Alertness
documents.body: Taken from Why We Sleep, here’s how alertness naturally varies throughout the day: Image Given this, you could argue that alertness follows a sawtooth pattern throughout the day. However, I think most people actually experience a sinusoidal pattern of alertness. Finally, most people would probably tell you they desire a square-wave pattern of alertness if it were reasonably achievable. Image Here’s my best attempt at doing so! AM: Get the blood flowing, caffeine + ⍺-GPC, and artificial sun exposure ASAP PM: Sleep stack + melatonin (and a whole routine in general) to prime the body for sleep Make this your #1 priority!

documents.label: Caffeine
documents.body: Despite popular opinion, caffeine is actually a very safe drug with tons of benefits and very few risks. As such, I’ve grown much more liberal with my intake of caffeine over the past few years. The biggest “risk” of caffeine is reduced sleep quality. This is definitely something I want to minimize. Analyzing my own average caffeine consumption throughout the day (see the sawtooth graph below), I go to sleep on approximately 110mg of caffeine. Obviously not ideal but 🤷‍♂️ . (source) Image

documents.body: I take a bunch of supplements every morning and evening to improve various aspects of my life. Examine.com is my favorite site for determining the efficacy of various supplements! This is how I originally curated my stacks in 2022. Because I also eat a highly restrictive diet, I take a greens blend (eg. Athletic Greens) and a daily men’s multivitamin. The efficacy of both of these are mixed so I view these more as insurance policies than anything. documents.label: Sleep Duration
documents.body: Contrarian opinion: I think most people actually get too much sleep! Yes, I’ve read Why We Sleep which makes a statistically rigorous argument for 8+ hours daily. However, studies also show that anywhere between 6-8 hours works. In fact, all cause mortality with 8 hours is actually higher than with 5 hours: (caveat: correlation vs causation) Image When I oversleep, I often feel more lethargic the following day yet have trouble going to sleep at the end of the night. I’ve found the right amount of sleep for me varies from anywhere between 5 hours and 7.5 hours (avg. 6.25h) per night depending on weight, exercise, season, etc.! What ChatGPT says about this ↑ Prompt: Why does the amount of sleep I need change depending on how much I weigh / whether I'm actively gaining or losing weight / the season? I'm a bodybuilder who bulks and cuts 20+ pounds per year, peaking in Jan (when I need the most sleep at 7+ hours) and at my lowest in the summer (when I only need like 5.5h) Your changing sleep needs are influenced by a combination of physiological, metabolic, and environmental factors related to your bodybuilding routines and seasonal rhythms. Here’s why:

documents.label: Getting Back On Track
documents.body: After travel, an outstanding weekend, or something else that kicks me off my normal routine, I’ve developed a simple strategy to get back on track. My top priority is always to get back to a good sleep schedule. In fact, I’ve even done 12-hour schedule flips (US ↔ India) without any jet lag whatsoever. How? Using supplements to modulate alertness: caffeine as an extender, the sleep stack with melatonin as a light switch. Take the time to learn how your body reacts to both and how you can then use them as tools to get back on track after disruption!

documents.label: The Human Side of AI: 5 Lessons from America’s Top AI Hubs
documents.body: The heart of AI innovation isn’t found in code — it’s found in conversation. That’s the belief that sparked The AI Collective, which started in early 2023 in a small San Francisco apartment. Today, it has grown into the largest AI community in the United States, with chapters in each of top ten AI hubs: Austin, Boston, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, New York City, San Francisco, Seattle, and Washington, DC. This year, I had the rare privilege of hosting in-person events in each of these cities, spending up to four days in each exploring their distinct cultures and vibrant AI communities. Unlike typical networking events, Collective gatherings are designed for meaningful connection. Members participate in intimate ten-person discussion groups, where we have lively and insightful conversations about AI’s most pressing topics. Through countless one-on-one and group conversations, I began to see patterns emerge — shared threads and distinct differences. Here are the five key le

documents.label: Top 10 Most Provoking Reads of 2024
documents.body: In a world addicted to the junk food of TikTok takes and bite-sized opinions, books stand apart as thoughtful distillations of humanity’s collective wisdom. They help us sharpen our perspectives, make sense of complexity, and uncover enduring value in a chaotic sea of fleeting distractions. Of the 70+ books I’ve read this year, these ten have stood out to me as uniquely thought-provoking — not because they aligned with my views, but because they challenged me to rethink them. Since I’m hopelessly indecisive when it comes to favorites, I haven’t ranked them. Instead, I’ve paired each with another title that adds nuance, contrast, or a fresh perspective to the conversation! This list is simply a fun way for me to share the ideas that resonated with me — and hopefully, they’ll resonate with you, too. documents.body: Venture capital as we know it is doomed. If your inner monologue just exclaimed “wow, that’s a bold claim” — you’re right! However, after talking with hundreds of fellow founders, operators, and investors during our weekly AI Collective community events, I have yet to hear a compelling counter to this claim in light of its supporting arguments. documents.label: The Apple Way
documents.body: Four lessons from working on the Apple Vision Pro team. The Apple Vision Pro will define a new paradigm in computing. As an AR/VR engineer working on VisionOS for the past two years and experiencing firsthand the breathtaking magic that is the VisionOS spatial computing platform, I can say this with the utmost confidence. How did we pull this off? What makes Apple so special? How has Apple secured its dominance as the most valuable company, most trusted and admired brand, and most notorious consumer product design house in the world? documents.body: Source: Midjourney V5 What do Joe Biden, Elon Musk, Barack Obama, Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping, Bill Gates, Warren Buffet, and Mark Zuckerberg all have in common? They are unanimously calling attention to the profound social, cultural, and even cosmic implications foreshadowed by the recent breakthroughs in artificial intelligence (AI). The line between creator and creation is blurring — challenging the very notion of what it means to be human. More existentially, many claim we are living on the precipice of life’s most significant evolution in its 3.7-billion-year history¹. While Google Research kicked off the gold rush in 2017, it was OpenAI that roused mass awareness when it released ChatGPT to the public last November². documents.label: Can ChatGPT Generate a Full iOS App?
documents.body: We already know that ChatGPT has the coding interview skills to land itself a job at a top tech firm. However, job interviews are a notoriously poor predictor of on-the-job performance. So, how would ChatGPT fare performing the day-to-day tasks of a tech worker? Is the software engineering profession under an imminent existential threat? As a mobile app developer, I wanted to understand ChatGPT’s ability to design and program large-scale applications. Can it piece together an entire project and transform mobile app development into an interactive, “choose your own adventure” experience? Can ChatGPT democratize app development — placing this valuable skill in the hands of the average layperson with an original idea? documents.label: From Nerd to Bodybuilder: Embracing Paradoxical Passions
documents.body: How does a shy nerd boy from high school find himself flexing on stage in front of hundreds of spectators donning little more than a G-string? Spray tanned and shaved from head to toe, I strode in front of the blinding spotlights as my name bellowed out over the PA system. Preparing to perform my solo posing routine, I masked first time jitters with a composed facade after hearing judges could sense fear like sharks smell blood in the water. Performing at a bodybuilding competition almost naked in front of a mass of ogling strangers was the culmination of a five-year journey. Once terrified at the mere thought of presenting a powerpoint in front of a small class, it hit me: how did I get here? I have been enthralled by computers and programming for as long as I can remember. Spending entire weekends squirreled away in my room, I taught myself how to write iOS applications, tinkered with Arduinos and bread board circuits, built custom computers, and reverse engineered electronic toys.

documents.label: Weightlifting App
documents.body: A gamified iOS app to tracks and analyze user workouts complete with intelligent feedback, online leaderboards. Contains multiple heuristic algorithms to gamify user progress via achievements and milestones.

documents.label: Liar's Dice
documents.body: Liar's Dice is a dice game that combines luck and skill as one must weigh probabilities with the game theory involved in predicting the decisions of other intellegent actors. I developed a simple tool to assist in deriving probabilities for each hand to aid in decision-making. This is exposed both as a simple React webpage as well as an API accessible by posting a POST request /api/v1/liarsdice/play.

documents.label: Web Experiments
documents.body: Web Experiments backend is a monorepo for my AWS EB-hosted online portfolio website along with Node / Express / PHP / MySQL backends for various other personal projects including Weightlifting App and ESPN Fantasy Football stats.

documents.label: Fantasy Basketball
documents.body: This app accesses basketball player data from a variety of online sources including espn.com, rotoworld.com, nba.com, and more for the purpose of tracking and evaluating NBA player performance. This app has almost all of the features of the official ESPN fantasy app and also includes additinal player discoery / insight features such as advanced player news and metrics.

documents.label: Weightlifting App ML
documents.body: A series of programs written in Python using Weightling App data to train a Keras deep learning model for the purpose of workout type prediction based on the exercises performed.

documents.label: Rotoworld ML
documents.body: A series of programs written in Python using the Rotoworld mobile API to train a Keras deep learning model for the purpose of evaluating NBA players based on tokenized news articles.
